setup_task: (Setup) Create text in two adjacent cells for a merge exercise
main_task: Merge cells A1 and B1, keeping the contents of the hidden cells
main_steps: Drag from cell A1 to cell B1 to select both cells.
In the Merge Cells dialog, select Keep the contents of the hidden cells.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Select cells A1 and B1.  
2) Go to Format > Merge Cells > Merge Cells or Merge and Center Cells.  
3) In the Merge Cells dialog, choose the option to hide the contents of the hidden cells.  
4) Click OK.

setup_task: (Setup) Create and format a 4x4 cell range for a new AutoFormat
setup_steps: Drag from cell A1 to cell D4.
Click Format in the menu bar.
Select a larger font size than the default.
main_task: Define a new AutoFormat named MyFormat from the formatted 4x4 range
main_steps: Drag from cell A1 to cell D4.
Click Format in the menu bar.
Type MyFormat in the Name box.
Verify that MyFormat appears in the Format list.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Select a cell range of at least 4x4 cells.  
2) Go to Format > AutoFormat Styles to open the AutoFormat dialog.  
3) Click Add.  
4) In the Name box of the Add AutoFormat dialog, type "MyFormat".  
5) Click OK.  
6) Click OK to close the AutoFormat dialog.

setup_task: (Setup) Create sample data for a standard filter with column labels
main_task: Apply a standard filter to show only rows where Qty is greater than 10
main_steps: Open the Field name list in the first filter row.
Open the Condition list in the first filter row.
Click the Value box in the first filter row.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select a cell within the data range containing the Qty column.  
2. Go to Data > More Filters > Standard Filter.  
3. In the Standard Filter dialog, under Field name, select the column that contains the Qty field.  
4. Under Condition, choose "greater than" (or ">", if available).  
5. In the Value field, enter 10.  
6. Click OK to apply the filter and display only rows where Qty is greater than 10.

setup_task: (Setup) Create sample data and a chart with a title
setup_steps: Complete the chart creation so a chart appears in the sheet.
main_task: Move the chart title to a different position
main_steps: Double-click the chart to enter edit mode.
Click the chart title to select it.
Press and hold the left mouse button on the selected title.
Drag the title to a different location within the chart.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Click on the chart title to select it.  
2) Press and hold the mouse button. The cursor changes to a move icon.  
3) Drag the title to the desired position.  
4) Release the mouse button when the title is in the desired location.  
5) Click outside the chart to exit selection mode.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a chart with one data series for single data label practice
setup_steps: Click Insert on the menu bar.
main_task: Insert a data label for only the Feb data point
main_steps: Click the data point for Feb once.
Click the same data point again.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Double-click the chart to enter edit mode. The chart should now be surrounded by a gray border.  
2) Click the Feb data point once, pause, then click again to select it.  
3) Right-click on the selected data point and choose Insert Single Data Label from the context menu.  
4) If desired, click outside the chart to leave edit mode.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a chart that can be resized
setup_steps: Insert a chart using the default chart option.
Finish the chart so it appears on the sheet.
main_task: Resize the chart interactively by dragging a corner handle
main_steps: Drag a corner selection handle outward to make the chart larger.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Click once on the chart to select it.  
2) Click and drag one of the corner selection handles until the chart reaches the desired size.  
3) When finished, click outside the chart to leave selection mode.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a cell with text and apply direct formatting
setup_steps: Click the Bold button on the toolbar.
main_task: Clear the direct formatting from the formatted cell using the Format menu
main_steps: Click Format on the menu bar.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Select the formatted cell or range of cells.  
2) Choose Format > Clear Direct Formatting from the Menu bar.

main_task: Open the Templates dialog with the keyboard shortcut
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
Press Ctrl+Shift+N to open the Templates dialog.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a named print range in the sheet
main_task: Select the named print range for printing and show it in print preview
main_steps: Open the Print Range drop-down list.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Go to Format > Print Ranges > Edit on the Menu bar to open the Edit Print Ranges dialog.  
2) Select the named print range from the Print Range drop-down list.  
3) Click OK to close the dialog.  
4) Open the Print dialog by choosing File > Print on the Menu bar or pressing Ctrl+P.  
5) The print preview will display only the named range. Click Print to proceed.

setup_task: (Setup) Create sample values for an error-checking spreadsheet
main_task: Create row totals and column totals, then show the difference between them
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Open the spreadsheet containing the data.  
2. Select the range of data to include in the pivot table.  
3. Go to the 'Insert' menu and choose 'Pivot Table'.  
4. In the Pivot Table dialog, confirm the data range and click 'OK'.  
5. In the Pivot Table field list, drag the row fields to the 'Rows' area.  
6. Drag the column fields to the 'Columns' area.  
7. Drag the values field to the 'Values' area.  
8. In the 'Values' area, click the dropdown arrow next to the value field and select 'Sum' to calculate row and column totals.  
9. Check the 'Show row totals' and 'Show column totals' options in the Pivot Table settings.  
10. To show the difference between row and column totals, create a new calculated field:  
    - Click on the 'Values' area, then click 'Add Calculated Field'.  
    - Enter a formula such as `Row Total - Column Total` (using the appropriate field names).  
    - Click 'OK' to add the difference field.  
11. The difference between row and column totals will now appear in the pivot table.
